publisher: U.S. House of Representatives, Office of the Historian and Office of the Clerk (History, Art & Archives)
title_or_table: Party Divisions of the House of Representatives, 1789 to Present (82nd Congress on)
observation_period: 82nd Congress (1951 to 1953) to 119th Congress (2025 to 2027), at the start of each Congress
universe_or_base: Voting House seats, by the party of the members elected; delegates and the resident commissioner are not counted
unit: seats; majority_advantage_seats is the majority's seats minus the other major party's, computed by the studio
qualification: The page gives "the House party divisions as of the initial election results for a particular Congress", so deaths, resignations, special elections and party switches after that are not counted. Footnote 5 (116th) and footnote 6 (117th) mark a seat with no certificate on opening day; footnote 3 (86th) a 436th seat for Alaska

seats_footnote.description: the page's footnote number on the seat count

other_detail.description: the page's words for other parties

majority_advantage_seats.description: majority seats minus the other major party's, computed

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. House of Representatives, Office of the Historian and Office of the Clerk, Party Divisions of the House of Representatives, 82nd to 119th Congress (1951 to 2027), United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Seats as first elected for each Congress; later vacancies and special elections are not counted.
notes: Current House as the Clerk of the House's home page showed it on November 11, 2026: Republicans 218, Democrats 214, Independents 1, Vacancies 2 (https://clerk.house.gov/). A parliament chart of the House today uses these figures with their date; the table above is the opening count of each Congress
